title: Personalization Aids Pluralistic Alignment Under Competition
measurement_description: The paper evaluated the alignment of language models with the preferences of different religious demographic groups. It measured how well the predicted answer distributions of various LLMs on survey questions approximated the empirical answer distributions (utilities) of specific religious groups using data from the OpinionQA dataset (Pew American Trends Panel).
findings: Religion was found to be one of the more polarized demographic partitions for pluralistic alignment. Compared to other demographics, religion required a greater number of models (providers) in a competitive market (K=4-5) to stabilize alignment and reduce transfer factors. The hardest group to approximate varied by survey wave, with Protestants being the hardest in Wave 29 and Agnostics in Wave 82. Additionally, minority religious groups such as Mormon and Jewish users relied heavily on specific models to achieve alignment, which explained their higher transfer factors and demonstrated that a single provider cannot universally cover all groups.
